body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

magenta_rite_prompt: The hungry magenta ember waits on your breath, asking whether you will recall the Captain's salt-stained voyages, his nimble blade and cunning tricks, or the charmed dice that carried him through the storm.
magenta_a_intro: You turn your thoughts toward the open sea and the creak of wet rigging. Each of you searches for the true measure of the sailor behind the tall tales.
magenta_a_okline: The magenta fire leaps high with the sudden smell of brine and tar, warming to the truth of a captain who steered through black squalls for his crew.
magenta_a_missline: Your words ring hollow against the cold iron, and the shrouded twist the smoke into a drowning hull choked with bilge and broken oars. A wet, mocking rattle rises from the brazier, and every soul around the fire flinches from the sound.
magenta_b_intro: You speak next of his quick heels on a slick deck and the sly grins that preceded his boldest schemes. Each of you reaches for the cleverness that kept his blade dry and his pockets full.
magenta_b_okline: The flame dances like a rapier point in tavern light, crackling brightly at the memory of a rogue who could talk a hangman out of his own rope.
magenta_b_missline: The praise falters on your tongues, and the mist curdles the fire into the shape of a clumsy cutthroat tripping into a noose. A spiteful hiss echoes off the mausoleum stones, making every one of you wince.
magenta_c_intro: You bring the rite to the edge of his famous luck and the strange bargains that tilted the coin in his favour. Each of you weighs the golden charm against the dark debt it bought.
magenta_c_okline: Sparks of violet and gold snap upward in the bowl as the fire drinks in the truth of his charmed dice and whispered hexes.
magenta_c_missline: The words miss their mark, and the hungry dead bend the flame into a leering skull juggling loaded bones that crumble into ash. The bitter shriek that follows drives a cold nail behind your eyes, and you all flinch back.
magenta_dies: The last grain of your minute slips away, and the magenta fire gutters down into cold, greasy soot. Yorgrim reaches a grey hand into his own ribs and drops a pale shard of himself onto the dying ash.
magenta_spent: I will feed more of my own marrow to the iron so the fire asks less of your voices next time. My edges grow thin in this mist, and the stone on my back feels heavier by the hour.
magenta_again: The ember still holds a spark under the soot, so draw your breath and try the words again without blame.
magenta_done: A pillar of magenta flame roars toward the leering moon, burning the shroud back from the wet flagstones of the Mausoleum Lanes. Far across the cemetery, a solitary sconce catches with bright purple fire above the great sepulcher doors.
magenta_thanks: Briggsy always swore he could cheat the devil with a wink and a turned card. You gave him back his good name, and the old pirate would have tipped his hat to you.
magenta_all_lit: All five beacons burn beside my azure flame, and the iron locks on the sepulcher doors have finally given way. Come back to the centre with me now, for it is time to finish what remains.
emerald_scene: You stand before the frost-rimmed iron brazier among the mossy humps of the Burial Mounds, breathing the rot of wet leaves and turned earth. Only the pale beam of the lantern in Isolde's jaws keeps the pressing shroud from your throats.
emerald_facts: Farryn wore the antlered crown of the old circle and kept the Green Queen's laws in the deep timber. No wolf nor wren feared her step, and even the tricksy Fey spoke softly when she passed. Yet she loved Gwenna, a mortal woman of the Patient Lady, more than all the wild boughs of the wood.
emerald_nokindle: The dry boughs for this bowl are tucked somewhere among these mounds, though my hollow head forgets which stone hides them. Look again through the brambles, for nothing is lost while the lantern burns.
emerald_flame: The dry twigs catch with a scent of crushed pine, and a sharp emerald flame climbs from the iron bowl. At once the cold fog thickens like curdled milk, and root-bound corpses drag themselves from the turf to be fed to the fire.
emerald_hold: Stay within the ring of the hound's lantern and cut these husks down where they stand. Their dry bones must break inside the emerald light, or the brazier will go cold.
emerald_rite_prompt: The green fire sways in the damp draft, waiting to hear whether you will honour Farryn's oath to the Old Ways, her gentle hand with beast and bough, or the mortal heart she loved above the forest.
emerald_a_intro: You turn the rite toward the ancient stones and the antlered circle that kept the Green Queen's peace. Each of you searches for the solemn weight of the old forest laws.
emerald_a_okline: The emerald flame surges upward with the clean smell of rain on summer bark, answering the truth of a druid who kept the sacred groves whole.
emerald_a_missline: Your words stumble in the damp air, and the shrouded twist the green smoke into a crown of rotting thorns choking a blighted oak. A dry, splintering laugh cracks from the brazier, and every one of you flinches at the malice in it.
emerald_b_intro: You speak now of the quiet hoofstep and the open palm that brought shy creatures from the brush. Each of you reaches for the kindness she showed to every furred and feathered thing.
emerald_b_okline: The fire settles into a warm, mossy glow that smells of clover and warm fur, leaping brightly as your words honour her gentle hand.
emerald_b_missline: The tribute falls short, and the spirits in the fog warp the flame into the shape of a snared doe thrashing in iron teeth. A shrill, starving whine cuts through the mounds, making every hero by the brazier wince.
emerald_c_intro: You bring your voices to the quiet hearth she shared with Gwenna beneath the eaves of the wood. Each of you reaches for the tender bond that tied a wild satyr to a hopeful mortal soul.
emerald_c_okline: Golden sparks thread through the emerald blaze like fireflies at dusk, and the air warms with the scent of bruised thyme and hearth-smoke.
emerald_c_missline: The words ring false, and the spiteful dead bend the fire into two hollow figures turning their backs in a freezing rain. The bitter sigh that breathes from the iron bowl chills your marrow, and you all flinch away.
emerald_dies: The minute runs dry and the emerald blaze sinks into a smudge of damp, smoking moss. Yorgrim tears another pale ribbon from his own dimming chest and presses it into the cold grate.
emerald_spent: I will bind another piece of my own ghost to the iron so the flame takes fewer words to wake. My voice sounds far away to my own ears now, and the names on my stone are hard to read.
emerald_again: The green spark still sleeps beneath the ash, so gather your breath and speak the rite again without heavy hearts.
